'''Atul Janardhan Butte'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brown University Library |url=https://library.brown.edu/theses/theses.php?task=search}}</ref> (August 26, 1969 – June 13, 2025) was an American [[Health informatics|biomedical informatician]], [[pediatrician]] and [[biotechnology]] entreprenuer. He was the Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg Distinguished Professor at the [[University of California, San Francisco]]. In 2015, Butte became the inaugural director of UCSF's Bakar Computational Health Sciences Institute.<ref name="Bole2015">{{cite web|last1=Bole|first1=Kristen|title=UCSF Taps Atul Butte to Lead Big Data Center|date=16 January 2015 |url=https://www.ucsf.edu/news/2015/01/122656/ucsf-taps-atul-butte-lead-big-data-center|access-date=8 June 2015|publisher=UCSF}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Butte was born in [[Philadelphia]] on August 26, 1969, to Janardhan Butte and Mangala Butte.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biomedical Informatician Atul Butte Dies at 55 |url=https://www.the-scientist.com/biomedical-informatician-atul-butte-dies-at-55-73095 |access-date=2025-06-17 |website=The Scientist |language=en}}</ref><ref name=thesis>{{Cite thesis |last=Butte |first=Atul J. |title=Exploring genomic medicine using integrative biology |date=2004 |degree=Thesis |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |hdl=1721.1/33680 |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/33680}}</ref> He attended [[Brown University]], where he studied computer science as an undergraduate student. As a member of the school's [[Program in Liberal Medical Education]] he was guaranteed acceptance to Brown's [[Alpert Medical School]], where he obtained his MD in 1995.

Butte completed a residency in pediatrics and a fellowship in pediatric endocrinology, both at [[Children's Hospital Boston]]. In 2004, he completed a [[Ph.D.]] from the [[Harvard–MIT Division of Health Sciences and Technology]], supervised by [[Isaac Kohane]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Atul Butte|url=http://www.xconomy.com/author/abutte/|publisher=xconomy|access-date=7 April 2013}}</ref>

Butte moved to California and became an assistant professor at Stanford University in 2005. He later became the Chief of the Division of Systems Medicine at [[Stanford University School of Medicine]] and [[Lucile Packard Children's Hospital]] where he held the position of an associate professor of pediatrics and (by courtesy) [[computer science]] and [[immunology]] & [[rheumatology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://med.stanford.edu/profiles/Atul_Butte/ |title=CAP - Atul Butte |access-date=2012-04-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419154933/http://med.stanford.edu/profiles/Atul_Butte/ |archive-date=2012-04-19 }}</ref> He moved to the [[University of California, San Francisco]] in 2015.

In April 2012, Butte delivered a [[TEDMED]] talk describing his lab's development of techniques using massive amount of publicly available biomedical research data to make new discoveries without running a wet-lab and actually [[outsourcing]] experiments using [[Scientist.com (company)|assaydepot.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tedmed.com/2012speakers|title=TEDMED - Speakers|website=TEDMED}}</ref>

Butte had an [[h-index]] of over 110 and was recognized by [[Publons]] as a highly cited researcher with over 70,000 citations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=NDyEvlQAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Atul J. Butte - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Atul Butte's Publons profile|url=https://publons.com/researcher/25193/atul-butte/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220207204837/https://publons.com/researcher/25193/atul-butte/|archive-date=2022-02-07|access-date=2022-02-07|website=publons.com|language=en}}</ref> He founded two biotechnology companies (Personalis<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.personalis.com/team.html |title=Personalis - Team |access-date=2012-04-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427202459/http://personalis.com/team.html |archive-date=2012-04-27 }}</ref> and NuMedii<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.numedii.com/company/team/team.html |title=Team |access-date=2012-04-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120228070505/http://numedii.com/company/team/team.html |archive-date=2012-02-28 }}</ref>) and wrote one of the first books on [[microarray]] analysis, ''Microarrays for an Integrative Genomics''.

== Personal life and death ==
Butte lived with his wife, Gini Deshpande, a cancer biology and biotechnology entrepreneur, and daughter in [[Menlo Park, California]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Leuty |first1=Ron |title=Big Data, new drugs: Peninsula company scores deal with Allergan |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/blog/biotech/2015/10/numedii-allergan-agn-big-data-psoriasis.html |website=www.bizjournals.com |access-date=26 January 2019 |date=2 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Big Data guru Atul Butte's NuMedii scores $3.5M VC round for 'digital' drug research {{!}} FierceBiotech |url=https://www.fiercebiotech.com/data-management/big-data-guru-atul-butte-s-numedii-scores-3-5m-vc-round-for-digital-drug-research |website=www.fiercebiotech.com |date=26 June 2013 |access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref> {{As of|2018}}, Deshpande was the [[chief executive officer]] of NuMedii, an [[artificial intelligence]] technology company.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.genomeweb.com/sequencing/numedii-inks-single-cell-sequencing-collaborations-yale-brigham-and-womens-hospital|title=NuMedii Inks Single-Cell Sequencing Collaborations With Yale, Brigham and Women's Hospital|last=<!--no byline-->|date=10 July 2018|work=GenomeWeb|access-date=12 July 2018|location=New York|url-access=registration}}</ref> His brother Manish J. Butte<ref name=thesis></ref> is a pediatrician at [[University of California, Los Angeles]].

Butte died in California on June 13, 2025, at the age of 55.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Muoio |first=Dave |date=2025-06-16 |title=Bioinformatics pioneer Atul Butte dies at 55 |url=https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/health-tech/atul-butte-computational-bioinformatics-pioneer-dies-55 |access-date=2025-06-17 |website=www.fiercehealthcare.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Simone |first=Michelle |date=2025-06-17 |title=University of California Health mourns the loss of Dr. Atul Butte, a renowned scientist and visionary leader |url=https://ucnet.universityofcalifornia.edu/employee-news/university-of-california-health-mourns-the-loss-of-dr-atul-butte-a-renowned-scientist-and-visionary-leader/ |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=UCnet |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Atul Janardhan Butte |url=https://www.skylawnmemorialpark.com/obituaries/atul-butte/obituary |website=[[Skylawn Memorial Park (San Mateo, California)|Skylawn Memorial Park]] |access-date=7 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250704142148/https://www.skylawnmemorialpark.com/obituaries/atul-butte/obituary |archive-date=4 July 2025}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2013, Butte was recognized as an Open Science Champion of Change by the [[White House]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bioinformatics Leader Honored by White House, Atul Butte - Stanford Medicine Children's Health |url=https://www.stanfordchildrens.org/en/about/news/releases/2013/bioinformatics-leader-honored-atul-butte.html |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=www.stanfordchildrens.org |language=en-us}}</ref> In 2015, he was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-03-01 |title=Nine UC members elected to the National Academy of Medicine {{!}} UC Health |url=https://health.universityofcalifornia.edu/2015/10/19/nine-uc-members-elected-to-the-national-academy-of-medicine/ |access-date=2024-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301202654/https://health.universityofcalifornia.edu/2015/10/19/nine-uc-members-elected-to-the-national-academy-of-medicine/ |archive-date=2019-03-01 }}</ref> In 2021, Butte was elected as a [[ISCB Fellow|Fellow]] of the [[International Society for Computational Biology]].<ref name="iscb-fellow">{{cite web |title=March 02, 2021: ISCB Congratulates and Introduces the 2021 Class of Fellows! |url=https://www.iscb.org/iscb-news-items/4626-2021-march02-iscb-congratulates-introduces-2021-class-fellows |website=www.iscb.org |access-date=17 June 2022}}</ref> In 2022, he became a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 AAAS Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |url=https://www.aaas.org/page/2022-fellows-0 |access-date=2024-11-23 |website=www.aaas.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, he received the Award for Excellence in Molecular Diagnostics from the [[Association for Molecular Pathology]] and the [[Morris F. Collen Award of Excellence]] from the [[American College of Medical Informatics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Recipients |url=https://www.amp.org/membership/awards-grants-honors/amp-award-for-excellence-in-molecular-diagnostics/past-recipients/ |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=Association for Molecular Pathology |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Atul Butte, MD, PhD, FACMI, to be awarded Morris F. Collen Award of Excellence at the AMIA 2024 Annual Symposium {{!}} AMIA - American Medical Informatics Association |url=https://amia.org/news-publications/atul-butte-md-phd-facmi-be-awarded-morris-f-collen-award-excellence-amia-2024 |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=amia.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, he was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-10 |title=Atul J. Butte {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/atul-j-butte |access-date=2025-10-11 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref>
